title: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants
description: Jesus tells of a man who planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug out a winepress and built a watchtower. Then he leased it to tenant farmers and went abroad. When the harvest time approached, he sent his servants to collect the fruit, but the tenants beat some, killed others and stoned the rest. He sent more servants, but they were treated the same way. Finally he sent his own son, saying, "They will respect my son." But the tenants said, "This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance!" So they seized him, threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. Jesus asks what the owner of the vineyard will do, and answers that he will give the vineyard to others who will bear its fruit. He quotes Scripture: "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone." The kingdom of God will be taken from them and given to a people who produce its fruits. The chief priests and the Pharisees understood that he was speaking about them, and wanted to arrest him, but they feared the crowd.

versions.title: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants
versions.description: A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug out a winepress and built a watchtower, then he leased it to tenant farmers and went abroad. When harvest time came, he sent his servants to collect the fruit, but the tenants beat them and killed some of them. Finally he sent his own son: "My son they will respect." But the tenants said: "This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, so that we may get his inheritance." Jesus asks: What will the owner of the vineyard do to them? He will give the vineyard to others. The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. The kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a people who produce its fruit. The chief priests and the Pharisees understood that he was speaking about them.
